findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes
findings.description: Commit markers appear as `- [ ] Commit: ...` sub-items at lines 105, 135, 179, 197, 212 and 224. The required form is a plain `**Commit**:` line, never a checkbox. A checkbox can be checked off by the task-checker, which makes the commit look like a work item. There are also six commits for a small slice. The one after Task 7 sits on a signal nothing consumes yet. The ones after Tasks 11 and 12 are test-only. Convert them to plain `**Commit**:` lines and keep them at working, tested points. Reasonable points are after Task 5 (parser), after Task 10 (wiring and CLI), and after Task 12 (regression tests). Drop the rest.

findings.title: Editing the shared fixture contradicts the slice's regression criterion and widens the blast radius
findings.description:
Slice success criterion (slice design lines 280-282) says `[ ]`/`[x]`/`[X]` behavior is proven byte-identical "by the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture tests continuing to pass unchanged."
- Task 1 appends two entries to that fixture.
- Task 5 (lines 95-98) then rewrites the existing `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` assertions from 5/3 to 7/5.
- Those edits mean the existing tests do not pass unchanged.
- Any other test that consumes this fixture and counts entries is exposed. Only Task 13's full run would catch that, after the Task 5 commit.

The slice design explicitly allows "or add a sibling fixture" (slice design line 222). A sibling fixture such as `sample-slice-plan-deprecated.md` keeps the existing assertions and the "byte-identical" proof intact. It also removes the need for the separate regression test added in Task 5 (lines 99-102), which duplicates the existing tests.

findings.title: `arch-status-vs-plans` has no test, though the success criterion names it
findings.description: The slice criterion (slice design lines 277-279) says both `plan-status-vs-entries` and `arch-status-vs-plans` must not false-positive. The slice design places both rules at `ConsistencyChecker.ts:726,749,828,849`. Task 12 covers only `plan-status-vs-entries`, and the Task 13 walkthrough also checks only `cf check` on a plan. Either add one `arch-status-vs-plans` case to Task 12, or state in the task that it is covered transitively and why. As written, that half of the criterion is unmet.

findings.title: Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change is not in the slice design and has no test
findings.description: Decision 4 calls for "the same one-line addition" to the inline `deriveEntryStatus()` call. The extra edit to the line-91 initializer, which adds a nested ternary, traces to no success criterion. Task 10 has no case that makes `detectDocuments` throw, so the new branch is untested. The task's own text admits the try block already resolves the normal case. The initializer is also a fallback path, and the project rules ask that failure paths be observable and tested. Either drop this sub-item, or keep it and add a test that forces the filesystem-error path and asserts `deprecated`.

findings.title: Task list is heavier than the change: over-granular and restates the design's code
findings.description:
Tasks 2, 3 and 4 are three small edits to one file (`slicePlanParser.ts`) and one logical change, with no tests between them. Merge them into one task. Tasks 2-4, 6, 8 and 9 also repeat the expression-level code that Decisions 1-4 of the slice design already give, plus "~line N" references that will go stale. Replace those with a pointer to the decision. Smaller trims:
- The third bullet in Task 7 (lines 131-132) only re-runs existing tests and is not a new test.
- The complementary `in-progress` case in Task 12 (lines 205-209) guards a behavior no success criterion names.
- Task 1's note (lines 46-50) is rationale rather than a step.

With these changes the list drops from 13 tasks to roughly 8-9 without losing any criterion coverage.

findings.title: Task 8 is separated from its test
findings.description: The order is Task 8 (navigator wiring), Task 9 (CLI wiring), Task 10 (tests for Task 9), then Task 11 (test for Task 8). That breaks the test-with pattern for Task 8. Reordering to 8, 11, 9, 10 fixes it. There are no dependency problems or cycles. Task 11's stop-and-report instruction on failure is reasonable.

findings.title: Success-criteria coverage
findings.description:
These criteria each map to a task:
- Indexed and unindexed `[~]` parsing maps to Tasks 1-3 and 5.
- `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` arithmetic maps to Tasks 4 and 5.
- `cf list slices` rendering and `isNext` map to Tasks 9 and 10.
- `cf next` and `findFirstNotCompleteEntry` skipping a `[~]` entry maps to Tasks 8 and 11.
- The `plan-status-vs-entries` rule not false-positiving on a deprecated entry maps to Task 12.

Apart from the findings above, no task falls outside the slice scope. The slice states no NFRs, so no load-test or CI-gating task is needed.

structured_findings.summary: Commit markers are written as checkboxes
Editing the shared fixture contradicts the slice's regression criterion and widens the blast radius
`arch-status-vs-plans` has no test, though the success criterion names it
Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change is not in the slice design and has no test
Task list is heavier than the change: over-granular and restates the design's code
Task 8 is separated from its test
